_comment: Companions (M7). archetypes: the sorts of people who will travel with you: their classes and background, their values (what they like and hate you doing, see values), what they want (pay, a share of the loot, a cause, knowledge, revenge), where they are found (inn, company), and how often. values: deed tags each value likes or hates (the game tags what you do: mercy, execution, theft...). wage: copper a day, base plus per level; share: part of the loot money for those who want loot. loyalty: 0 to 100; below 'complain' they grumble, below 'desert' they may leave in the night (taking something), above 'devoted' they will follow you anywhere. lines: what they say ({name} is the speaker, {leader} you).

sellsword.name: sell-sword
story: Fought for three lords and was paid by one.
Left a free company after a quarrel over a dead man's boots.
Has a scar for every border in the region.

old_soldier.name: old soldier
story: Too old for the lord's levy, too stubborn to stop.
Buried a whole company in the last war and walked home alone.

hedge_wizard.name: hedge wizard
story: Was thrown out of a circle of mages for asking the wrong questions.
Taught themselves from a stolen book, and it shows.

wandering_priest.name: wandering priest
story: Walks the roads to tend the dying where no priest will go.
Left a rich temple to do what the god actually asked.

zealot.name: zealot
story: Hunts witches, and has found a great many.
Burned the heretics of their own village, and would do it again.

cutpurse.name: cutpurse
story: Owes money to people who break fingers.
Grew up in the gutters and means never to go back.

outlaw_hunter.name: outlaw hunter
story: Bandits burned the family farm; they have been hunting bandits since.
Lost a brother on the road and wants the men who did it.

runaway_serf.name: runaway serf
story: Ran from a cruel lord's fields, with his bailiff's blood on their hands.
Wants to see the high and mighty brought low.

hired: "I'll get my things. They won't take long."
"Pay me on time and you'll have no trouble from me."
approve: {name} nods, as if something has been settled.
disapprove: "That was wrong, and you know it."
complain: "I'm starting to wonder why I'm here."
{name} walks apart from the rest of you today.
"There are other roads, you know. Other people to walk them with."
unpaid: "My purse is as light as yesterday. Lighter."
"We agreed on a wage. I remember. Do you?"
desert: In the morning {name} is gone, and so is some of your coin.
{name} slipped away in the night. They did not go empty-handed.
leave: "Well. It was something." {name} shoulders their pack and goes.
{name} takes their pay and walks off without looking back.
devoted: {name} has stopped counting the days. They will follow you anywhere now.
battle: {name} spits on their hands and grips their weapon.
road: {name} walks in silence for a mile, then says something about the weather that is not about the weather.
{name}: "My father walked this road. Said it was shorter then."
{name} asks whether {leader} has thought about what happens when this is over.
{name} hums the same four notes until somebody says something.
{name}: "If I stop, I will not start again. So I am not stopping."
{name} points out a bird, or a track, or a broken fence, and reads more into it than seems likely.
{name}: "Do you smell that? ... No? Right. Nothing, then."
{name} adjusts a strap for the fourth time this hour.
{name} says nothing for so long that when they speak it makes everyone jump.
road_tired: {name} has been limping for a while and saying nothing about it.
{name}: "When we stop, I am not getting up again for a week."
road_wet: {name} pulls their hood down further and says something about the country and its weather.
road_night: {name} keeps looking behind you, and says it is nothing.
{name}: "We should have stopped an hour ago."
{name} walks closer than they did in daylight.
camp: {name} stares into the fire and says nothing for a long time.
{name} tells a story about a pig, a priest and a flooded ford. Nobody laughs; everybody grins.
{name} checks their gear twice before sleeping.
"Strange country, this. I don't like the quiet."
level_up: "I'm getting better at this. Don't tell anyone."
{name} moves like someone who has survived a lot of mornings.
mood_good: "Better than I've been in years, if you want the truth."
mood_bad: "Since you ask: not well. Not well at all."
